ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Year-one academic writing, presentation, inquiry and ethical engagement.

MCCMEDI111.name: Introduction to Film & Media
MCCMEDI111.contribution: introduces the study of film and media, tracing the historical development of cinema and the elements of film form (narrative, cinematography, editing, sound) and treating media as cultural forms that reflect and shape society; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's media and digital-culture analysis by supplying the analytical vocabulary, although its main object is film rather than digital media

MCCMEDI111.methods: Close film and media analysis; Historical and cultural contextualization; Application of feminist and postcolonial film theory; Independent analytical or creative-analytical media research

MCCMEDI112.name: Media Archaeology
MCCMEDI112.contribution: studies how pre-digital media technologies such as cassette tapes, typewriters and printed books shaped the production, circulation and preservation of knowledge, through material analysis and historical interpretation; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's history-of-ICT component (ICT Revolutions: Continuity and Change) but addresses earlier media technologies rather than the digital revolution itself

MCCMEDI211.name: From T.V. to TikTok
MCCMEDI211.contribution: examines how television, film, podcasts and TikTok narratives shape social attitudes and everyday life, treating viral moments as cultural snapshots of contemporary values and anxieties; it directly engages the social-media and digital-culture content of the target's Digital Cultures, although from an American mainstream-media perspective
MCCMEDI211.topics: Media storytelling and power; American everyday life; 1950s television and conformity; Science fiction and social anxieties; Media futures and marginalization; Indigenous representation and self-representation; Disability stereotypes and visibility; Authentic voice and cultural agency; Future foresight and inclusive scenarios

MCCMEDI212.name: Media & the Environment
MCCMEDI212.contribution: analyses how film, photography, sound and digital media make ecological processes and environmental risk visible and shape how environmental problems are understood; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the link between media and the planet in the target's technology, people and planet identity
MCCMEDI212.topics: Environmental representation; Anthropocene; Animal representation and human-nonhuman relations; Deep time and ecological temporality; Biocentrism and environmental justice; Contested ideas of nature; Indigenous and postcolonial media; Ecological risk and scientific knowledge; Environmental affect and perception; Agency, scale and responsibility; Sustainability discourse

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: teaches data cleaning, manipulation and visualization for tabular, spatial and text data with hands-on examples from the sciences, social sciences and humanities, and ends in an own research project applying data analysis to a research question; it offers related content for introductory data handling and analysis for social questions, the basis of the target's Working with Big Data and data-science content

DISGATE101.name: Introduction to Programming
DISGATE101.contribution: teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python with testing and debugging; it offers a partial contribution to the basics of coding that the programme page names for the target's Introduction to Digital Technologies I, although it is a computer-science gateway course rather than a digital-society course

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.contribution: examines the ethics of AI (fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility and accountability, the moral status of AI systems, existential risk and political implications) together with the psychology of AI; it offers related content for the target's digital-ethics and generative-AI-and-society direction

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis

options.label: Digital Media, Society and AI
options.labelReason: The plan integrates media history, cultural analysis, experimental communication and digital publics with AI ethics, the social and economic impacts of AI, and methods for studying policy and data. Creative Communication Laboratory contributes digitally mediated expression alongside other experimental forms. The computing courses provide practical understanding of the technologies under study.
options.concept: Study how media, AI and digital systems shape public debate, organisations and everyday life. Combine media analysis and creative work with sociology, AI ethics, economics and policy analysis. Use programming, data analysis and research methods to investigate social questions.
progression: Introductory media and sociology precede advanced study of media narratives and publics. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Statistics & Experimental Methods, and data handling precedes Machine Learning. Programming precedes advanced algorithms and optimisation.
traceOverrides: analyses how film, photography, sound and digital media make ecological processes and environmental risk visible and shape how environmental problems are understood; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's media analysis and to the environmental side of Social and Environmental Impacts of the Digital Economy, although its focus is environmental representation

options.label: Data, Algorithms and AI in Society
options.labelReason: The completed curriculum has twelve courses in programming, computer science, AI, data science and mathematics (Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, AI Ethics, Decision-making in AI, Optimization Methods in AI, Networks & Operating Systems, Database Management Systems, Algorithms & Data Structures and Probability & Statistics), three on research methods and statistics (Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods and Qualitative Research Methodology), and eight on the social, ethical and behavioural side (Ethics, Human Rights, Persuasive Communication, From T.V. to TikTok, Media Archaeology, Calling Bullshit, Marketing & Consumer Engagement and Behavioral Economics), plus Personal & Professional Development. The label names the technical majority first and the social and behavioural perspectives second; it does not claim a full computer-science or data-science degree.
options.concept: Study the technologies behind digital life through programming, networks, databases, machine learning and AI. Use media studies, ethics and behavioural economics to ask how these technologies influence choices and participation.
options.distinctness: This option uses 8 different courses to deepen networks, databases, mathematical statistics, AI decision-making and neural networks, and add behavioural economics and digital marketing. The first option devotes more courses to sociology, media interpretation, public policy, creative practice and the social impacts of AI.
progression: Programming precedes networks, algorithms and advanced AI. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics and Neural Networks & Deep Learning. Data Science precedes Machine Learning, and Research Methods & Statistics precedes the later applied statistics and behavioural economics courses.
traceOverrides: examines the ethics of AI (fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility and accountability) together with the psychology of AI; it offers related content for the ethical analysis of algorithmic and generative-AI systems that complements the technical courses in this programme

analysis: The broad option links substantial digital content rather than merely assembling unrelated disciplines. Media Archaeology traces print, broadcasting, computing and networks. From T.V. to TikTok applies narrative analysis to mainstream American media, including digital platforms. Social theory includes digital publics and a civil-society group project. AI Ethics studies fairness, privacy and responsibility, while Business & Economy in the Age of AI addresses adoption, innovation, work, distribution and governance. Creative Communication Laboratory adds experimental writing, sonic forms and some digitally mediated expression. Public Policy Analysis adds policy memos and comparative policy reasoning through a non-digital case. Film foundations, rights, comparative politics, persuasion and general ethics remain complementary. Calling Bullshit develops practical misinformation detection and a video project. The quantitative and qualitative methods courses support social inquiry. Data cleaning, prediction, algorithms and optimisation are technical tools rather than a substitute for analysis of their social use. The second option adds networks, SQL and relational authorisation, theoretical statistics, AI decision-making under uncertainty and deep learning. Its Behavioural Economics course directly contributes experimental reasoning about biases, and Marketing & Consumer Engagement adds digital marketing applications. Eight courses differ in each direction. The two options therefore differ both by weight and through different enquiries. A new general business, sustainability, politics or media plan would rely on the same few dedicated digital intersections or dilute the subject. Maastricht retains a distinct integrated sequence in digital politics and regulation, virtual worlds, critical making and individual research. No required UCR capstone is claimed.

candidateDecisions.label: Data, algorithms and AI as technical objects of digital society
Sustainable digital futures and post-growth society
candidateDecisions.reason: Media & the Environment and Business & Economy in the Age of AI offer specific intersections. Sustainability and governance courses add context, while the available study of environmental impacts of digital systems is concentrated in courses already used by the broad option.

candidateDecisions.label: Psychology and human decision-making
candidateDecisions.reason: Behavioural Economics, Statistics & Experimental Methods and persuasion provide meaningful human-decision study, but the digital application is concentrated in courses already used by the technical option.

candidateDecisions.label: Law, policy and rights
candidateDecisions.reason: Human Rights, Public Policy Analysis and AI Ethics provide legal, policy and ethical study. Their combination offers limited dedicated digital law, and the closest option already incorporates their strongest contributions.

candidateDecisions.label: Arts, heritage and intellectual traditions
candidateDecisions.reason: Media Archaeology and Introduction to Film & Media add historical and cultural interpretation. Available heritage and traditions courses have limited digital application beyond the closest option.

candidateDecisions.label: European studies, globalisation and development
candidateDecisions.reason: European politics and global development offer comparative institutional contexts, with too little sustained digital inquiry for another Digital Society option.

candidateDecisions.label: Gender and diversity
candidateDecisions.reason: Media & Race and sociology provide ways to study representation and exclusion, while a sustained pathway on digital identity and inequality would rely mainly on courses already used by the closest option.

candidateDecisions.label: Entrepreneurship
candidateDecisions.reason: Strategy & Digital Transformation, marketing and business AI support applied business study. The available dedicated digital courses largely share the technical or broad option’s questions, while general venture courses would shift the emphasis to business.

candidateDecisions.label: Sustainable healthcare
candidateDecisions.reason: Biomedical and health courses provide domain context, but the available AI ethics examples do not amount to a sustained digital healthcare curriculum.

candidateDecisions.label: Digital systems for social good and creative digital communication
candidateDecisions.reason: Creative Communication Laboratory supports creative experimentation and some digital forms. Media analysis and computing contribute different skills, with limited sustained production or civic design for a distinct third option.

candidateDecisions.label: Digital leadership, innovation and business transformation
candidateDecisions.reason: The strategy course covers planning and digital value, and business AI covers adoption. Together with marketing these make an applied cluster, but specialist depth in organisational digital change is limited and the closest option already addresses the main societal question.

candidateDecisions.label: Independent digital-society research
candidateDecisions.reason: Quantitative and qualitative research courses offer defensible methods in both options. Independent research is an additional opportunity and cannot justify a distinct taught Digital Society option.
